extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and scientific review officers (also useful for applicants seeking reviewer expectations)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance for peer reviewers and scientific review officers describing reviewer roles, evaluation criteria, meeting and scoring procedures, integrity/COI requirements, critique writing, and use of the Internet Assisted Review (IAR) system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of first-level peer reviewers (overall impact assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: First level peer reviewers assess the overall impact that a proposed project will likely have on the biomedical research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stipulated in the NIH Peer Review regulations (CFR 52h), an application must be approved by two levels of NIH peer review. To learn more about first level peer review see First Level: Peer Review | Grants & Funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity, confidentiality, and conflict-of-interest certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to certify that they understand the rules of integrity and confidentiality in the peer review process and the consequences for not following these rules; they must also certify before and after review meetings that all conflicts of interest (COI) were identified and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, NIH reviewers are required to take trainings in review integrity and bias awareness to participate in most NIH review meetings. Links: Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review; Managing Conflicts of Interest in NIH Peer Review of Grants and Contracts; Review Integrity and Bias Awareness Training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate applications using notice-specific review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must evaluate applications using the criteria established in the notice of funding opportunity to which an application(s) was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional guidance for how to evaluate individual criteria is available through standard reviewer guidance documents. See: Peer Review Criteria and Considerations; Consolidated List of Reviewer Documents - Review Criteria Information; Review Criteria Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of human subjects, vertebrate animals, and biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the meeting, the SRG will discuss any concerns with the use of human subjects, vertebrate animals, and/or biohazards within applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review panels should identify and discuss any ethical, safety, or regulatory concerns related to human subjects protections, animal welfare, or biohazards during SRG meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Group (SRG) meeting participation and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are brought together as a Scientific Review Group (SRG) to discuss the merits of the studies proposed in individual applications and submit a final impact score for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tip: watch a mock study section to learn how reviewers discuss applications (NIH Peer Review: “Live” Mock Study Section with Extended Q&A). See Meeting Overview and Roles for responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process: preliminary ratings and final overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are typically given a preliminary rating as part of assigned reviewers’ initial evaluations; however an application’s final rating or ‘overall impact score’ is determined by the entire review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Scoring in First Level Peer Review and Consolidated List of Reviewer Documents – Scoring Information for details on scoring rules and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing reviewer critiques and summary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer critiques are part of the summary statement and an important source of feedback for what reviewers liked and didn’t like about their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and examples for preparing critiques are provided in Reviewer Critique Information and Consolidated List of Reviewer Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Internet Assisted Review (IAR) for reviewer workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: IAR is a web-based module within NIH’s eRA Systems that reviewers use to view meeting materials, certify their confidentiality and COI forms, access applications and submit scores and critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IAR resources and how-to pages: Access IAR; Navigating IAR; Fill Out Personal Profile; Reviewer Reimbursement Info; Certify Pre-Meeting COI; Access Meeting Materials in IAR; Submit & Manage Critiques, Scores; View Other Reviewers’ Critiques; Submit Final Scores; Certify Post-Meeting COI in IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reviewer responsibilities in IAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must complete administrative tasks in IAR such as filling out a personal profile, certifying pre- and post-meeting COI, accessing meeting materials, submitting critiques and final scores, and reviewing other reviewers’ critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tasks are required steps in the review workflow and are supported by IAR online help and FAQs (For Reviewers: Navigating IAR; IAR for Reviewers Online Help).
